title: Radioactive decay: types and properties
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: N02-uk1#t3 term and clue written for the game; N02-uk1#t1 term and clue written for the game; N02-uk1#t4 term and clue written for the game; N02-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: N02-uk1#N.3, N02-uk1#N.9, N02-uk1#N.12, N02-uk1#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Alpha radiation
items.clue: Shown to be present when a sheet of paper causes a big drop in the reading.

items.label: Geiger–Müller tube
items.clue: Detector connected to a counter to record emissions from a radioactive source.

items.label: Gamma radiation
items.clue: Shown to be present when a reading remains after aluminium and is reduced by lead.

items.label: Background count
items.clue: Reading taken first, with no source present, then subtracted from every later reading.

questions.stem: A student measures a background count rate of 30 counts per minute. With a source in front of a GM tube she records these count rates, each counted over one minute, in counts per minute: no absorber 1530; paper 330; 5 mm aluminium 325; 25 mm lead 105. What does the source emit?
questions.explanation: Corrected: 1500, 300, 295, 75. Paper removes most counts (α). Aluminium changes almost nothing (no β). Lead reduces what is left (γ).

questions.stem: A GM tube 0.30 m from a γ source records 1250 counts per minute. The background count rate is 50 counts per minute. The tube is moved to 0.60 m from the source. What count rate does it now record?
questions.explanation: Corrected rate 1200; twice the distance → 1200 ÷ 4 = 300; recorded rate 300 + 50 = 350.

questions.stem: Technetium-99m emits γ rays only and has a half-life of 6.0 h. It is injected into patients so that the organs that take it up can be imaged by a γ camera outside the body. Which statement is a correct reason for choosing technetium-99m?

options.text: Its γ rays are strongly ionising, so they give a strong signal at the camera.
Its half-life is short because so little is injected, and a small sample halves quickly.
Its γ rays make the organ's own tissue radioactive, so that the organ shows up.
Its γ rays are weakly ionising and most pass out of the body to the camera.

questions.stem: A worker's radiation badge holds a strip of photographic film behind four windows: open; thin plastic (stops α, like paper); 3 mm of aluminium; 2 mm of lead. After a month, the film is equally dark behind the open window and the plastic, much fainter behind the aluminium, and slightly fainter still behind the lead. Which radiations reached the badge?
questions.explanation: No change at the plastic: no α. The big drop at the aluminium shows β. Some darkening remains behind the aluminium and lead: γ.
